articles.title: Pokemon: Diamond and Pearl Box Set 1 - IGN
articles.summary: This is not going to go down in history as a leap forward in animation. Honestly, for all it's a decent kids' show, it's not even at the point where adults are going to be able to watch it for more than a couple of minutes without getting restless. In 20-odd years, though, when the kids of today start feeling '00s nostalgia and make the mistake of trying to enjoy the cartoons of their youth, they probably won't feel quite as bad as we do when we realize how awful M.A.S.K. was.
articles.body:
If you grew up in the '80s, like a lot of you probably did, the DVD era may have had some unintended consequences for you. A lot of the TV cartoons we loved as children are out on DVD now, and if you buy those DVDs and watch them today, you know what you'll find out? Those shows were bad .

Seriously. Horrible. They looked like hacked-out crap and they were terribly written even if you take into account the fact that they were designed for the sole purpose of selling toys to six-year-olds. Transformers nostalgia runs rampant around the internet, but you might notice that it tends to focus on the toys more than the show. That's because the Transformers show was godawful, and Transformers was one of the good ones, the ones with a budget and some talent behind them. Pick up the Galaxy High School box set and see how many episodes you can sit through before you pass out and choke to death on your own vomit.

What does this have to do with Pokemon ? Well, it helps to give a show like this a little historical perspective. On a mechanical level, Pokemon today is what Jayce and the Wheeled Warriors was 20-some years ago (just to pull an example out of a hat). It's the advertising/entertainment arm of a multi-pronged marketing enterprise – another toy commercial, although the toys are a lot more complicated than they used to be. It may not be great entertainment, especially if you're more than six years old, but it does its job better than, say, Rubik the Amazing Cube did.

These two discs feature the first 17 episodes of Diamond and Pearl , the latest evolution of the series, based on the new Nintendo DS videogame. Brock and Ash are back, but Misty is gone. She's been replaced by Dawn, a fresh face dedicated to succeeding her mother as a Pokemon Coordinator. "Coordinating" Pokemon goes one step beyond simply training them – Dawn's ultimate ambition seems to involve winning the Pokemon equivalent of the Miss America competition, but if I'm wrong I'm sure some six-year-old will rapidly be able to correct me.

Despite those kinds of superficial changes, Pokemon is still more or less the same show on a mechanical level. Our heroes wander around the world, join competitions, encounter rivals (more than a decade after their debut, Team Rocket are still our heroes' perennial opponents), and admire lots of different kinds of cute monster antics. The addition of all the new Diamond and Pearl monsters (on top of the Gold and Silver monsters and the now-old-school original 100 from Red and Blue) gives the show a gigantic array of Pokemon to pick from, and the old favorites haven't been sacrificed just to give the new monsters extra promotion.

That's the real draw of the series, of course. The people involved aren't very interesting – they're just more cartoon humans, and they act like one-note cartoon humans have since the dawn of color television. (Not to mention, the "best by" date on James' raving queen act sailed past us maybe five or six years ago.)

The monsters, on the other hand, are the unpredictable part, and the show makes the most of them. Digital animation nowadays lets you produce a good-looking TV show on a shoestring. The visual style of Pokemon hasn't changed a whole lot, but Diamond and Pearl has a much sharper picture and much smoother animation, which does a lot for the newer, more detailed monster designs.

"Pokemon" is the name on the marquee, and that aspect of the series is still a lot of fun. The better episodes on these discs come up with more for them to do then just fight with each other, while the weaker ones still make the most of the monsters' innate visual charm. When you think about it, the best of all possible Pokemon TV shows might be one without any humans in it at all. At the very least, it would save on the cost of voice actors

The 17 episodes included on this box set are split up on only two discs, but given that they're dual-layer discs, there's only one voice track, and the episodes are presented in an ordinary 4:3 TV aspect ratio, there are enough bits to go around and keep the show looking good. The picture is sharp and all the day-glo kids'-show colors are bright and inviting without seeming too garish or weird. (Well, they might seem garish or weird if you're over the age of 30, but in that case we can't help you.)

As mentioned above, there's only one voice track here, with the Viz-produced English dub. This is not a show that will demand any extra effort from your sound system, but the dub is surprisingly good. The actors behind most of these characters have been voicing them for years now – Addie Blaustein is great at delivering Meowth's snarky dialogue -- and the script actually features a smoother rewrite job than some shows that are supposed to be aimed at a more mature audience.

While most anime publishers are slimming down their packages as much as possible these days, the Diamond and Pearl sets are sticking with an old-fashioned format. Each disc comes in its own plastic keepcase (with monster profiles on the back covers, besides just the episode listing), and the two fit into a cardboard slipcase.

On the discs themselves, there's nothing extra to speak of at all. This still isn't that bad a deal, though – the suggested retail price for this set is only $25, and you can get it at a discount all over the place.

This is not going to go down in history as a leap forward in animation. Honestly, for all it's a decent kids' show, it's not even at the point where adults are going to be able to watch it for more than a couple of minutes without getting restless. In 20-odd years, though, when the kids of today start feeling '00s nostalgia and make the mistake of trying to enjoy the cartoons of their youth, they probably won't feel quite as bad as we do when we realize how awful M.A.S.K. was.

articles.title: 'Similar Art Styles Make the Comparisons Inevitable' — Palworld and Pokémon Fans Are Arguing Over Whether New Whale Pal Panthalus Copies Kyogre
articles.summary: Palworld and Pokémon fans are arguing over whether a new whale Pal called Panthalus copies the Pokémon, Kyogre.
articles.body:
Palworld and Pokémon fans are arguing over whether a new whale Pal called Panthalus copies the Pokémon, Kyogre.

Palworld creature Panthalus is a massive legendary blue-green whale with a white belly, flared fins and tribal-like markings across its body, plus a large bronze decoration. Beloved Pokémon Kyogre, meanwhile, is a legendary blue whale with a white belly, flared fins and tribal markings across its body, with no bronze decoration.

Writing on social media, some fans have said that the design of Panthalus is "clearly inspired" by Kyogre, even if the concept of a mythical whale is not unique to Pokémon. One fan dubbed the design as "brazen," though others said it looked "legally distinct" enough.

"I feel like the similar art styles make the comparisons inevitable," tweeted video game content creator Josh Scorcher. "Like, Game Freak doesn't own the concept of a legendary/divine whale creature... But you have to be incredibly dishonest to not immediately think of Kyogre when you see this."

Others, however, have dismissed the comparison. "Literally the only thing they have in common is that they're both whales," one fan said . "Panthalus looks NOTHING like Kyorge," another added . "Concept is there, but I can easily visually distinguish them."

oh my god the people saying panthalus doesnt even RESEMBLE kyogre are coping so unbelievably hard bro pic.twitter.com/1Ph4IJR39Q — Decaticon (@Decaticon) July 14, 2026

oh my god the people saying panthalus doesnt even RESEMBLE kyogre are coping so unbelievably hard bro pic.twitter.com/1Ph4IJR39Q

This pal is clearly inspired by Kyogre which isn't inherently a bad thing. However because palworld creatures are mostly inspired by pokemon it makes their designs feel pretty uninspired. Palworld's designs would greatly benefit from taking more inspiration outside of pokemon pic.twitter.com/dA5Jv0waP9 — doodlelotl (@Doodlelot) July 14, 2026

This pal is clearly inspired by Kyogre which isn't inherently a bad thing. However because palworld creatures are mostly inspired by pokemon it makes their designs feel pretty uninspired. Palworld's designs would greatly benefit from taking more inspiration outside of pokemon pic.twitter.com/dA5Jv0waP9

Sind sich zu ähnlich⁉️ Panthalus 🐳, ein Pal aus Palworld von Pocketpair Inc. & Kyogre 🐋, ein Pokemon von Gamefreak / Nintendo #pokemon #palworld pic.twitter.com/2XQhZXWNvv — PokéTen @Eurofurence 30 (@poketen_) July 15, 2026

Sind sich zu ähnlich⁉️ Panthalus 🐳, ein Pal aus Palworld von Pocketpair Inc. & Kyogre 🐋, ein Pokemon von Gamefreak / Nintendo #pokemon #palworld pic.twitter.com/2XQhZXWNvv

Panthalus' introduction comes just as fans discovered that several other Pal species have quietly had their designs changed in Palworld's big 1.0 update . Despite hundreds of other additions and tweaks being listed in developer Pocketpair's patch notes, there was curiously no mention of alterations to Verdash, Robinquill, Fengallop, and Grintale, which previously displayed more distinct similarities to familiar Pokémon species Cinderace, Decidueye, Cobalion, and Galarian Meowth.

IGN contacted Pocketpair for comment about these changes, but received no response.

Comparisons between Palworld's Pal designs and Pokémon are nothing new, of course, and fans have been pointing out similarities between species since before Palworld's original launch, when many accused Pocketpair of "ripping off" Pokémon designs.

And of course, all of this comes amid the ongoing legal battle between The Pokémon Company and Pocketpair over the use of patents, which seemingly prompted the latter to make gameplay changes in order to nullify its claims. A judgment is expected later this year .

Palworld's 1.0 launch landed earlier this month, finally bringing the game out of early access. Pocketpair said at the time that it would not raise the game's price beyond $29.99 as Palworld has "become a success beyond our wildest dreams." That statement likely reflects the fact that more than 40 million players have dipped their paws into Palworld since its early access launch.

Our Palworld Interactive Map has been updated for 1.0, including Watchtower Locations , so you can make sure to uncover everything new. We’ve also got a guide to 1.0 Pal Breeding Combos and How to Get Hardwood , plus the Best 1.0 Mounts to Catch in Order , and the Fastest Flying Mounts in 1.0 .

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: The Original Pokémon Series Is Now Streaming on Disney+ — So Where Are All of the Episodes?
articles.summary: The original Pokémon TV series is officially streaming on Disney+. Some of it, at least.
articles.body:
The original Pokémon TV series is officially streaming on Disney+ . Some of it, at least.

Of the 80ish total episodes that comprise the original Indigo League arc , only 27 are now available on Disney+. That's not an entirely random number — the first season of Pokémon was split into three parts when it was brought to DVD in North America, and Disney's episode count lines up with what was included on Viz Media’s first compilation.

Netflix, which has long been the streaming home for most of the Pokémon series , continues to have the first 52 episodes. That number matches how the series was originally split up for annual North American broadcast schedules.

Unlike Netflix, which goes with the specific "Indigo League" title, the episodes on Disney+ can be found under the arc's broader title, “Pokémon the Series: The Beginning.” Both streaming services skip over the original 18th episode, “ Beauty and the Beach ,” which only aired a few times in the U.S. after some heavy editing.

You're not entirely out of luck if you're looking for the full 80-episode arc. Those last 26 episodes are available to stream for free with ads on YouTube and Tubi , and are also included in Warner Home Video's revamped DVD release from 2014.

Disney+ was already streaming most of the more recent Sun & Moon seasons as well as a small selection of Pokémon movies, including The Rise of Darkrai and Zoroark: Master of Illusions . The addition of the original arc marks the streamer’s first major move with the franchise since acquiring the streaming license earlier this year.

Disney also picked up the broadcast rights for the original series, meaning Pokémon is officially back on Disney XD schedules .

The Pokémon TV series has become pretty closely associated with Netflix, with the streamer even producing its own original series with the franchise, Pokémon Concierge . It’s not entirely clear what else Disney plans to do with its newly acquired streaming and broadcast rights, and whether we’ll ever get the full Indigo League arc (let alone the full series) on either streaming platform.

Pokémon as a whole is currently celebrating its 30th anniversary, which has naturally been a ripe occasion for announcements across all of the franchise's iterations. We're talking new TCG releases , plenty of Pokémon Go events , and even some LEGO sets .

Somewhat ironically, the mainline Pokemon games are actually skipping 2026, but we did get our hands on what I consider one of the best cozy games of the modern generation, Pokémon Pokopia . We also got our first look at Gen 10 , Winds and Waves, which included a glimpse at the three new starters .

Disney+ continues to chug along in its own right, though it no longer openly reports the number of subscribers across its particularly large number of plans and bundles . The company has recently been focused on diversifying what it offers through the Disney+ app, having just inked a deal with TikTok to bring user-made shorts to the service. The possibility of a free, ad-supported streaming option was mentioned during the company's most recent earnings call , but in the era of endless price hikes , I wouldn’t get too optimistic.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who, when she isn't following streaming news, spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: Krispy Kreme Is Getting 6 New Pokémon-Themed Donuts
articles.summary: Krispy Kreme has announced a Pokémon doughnut collection that will be available for a limited time starting August 18.
articles.body:
Krispy Kreme has announced a Pokémon doughnut collection that will be available for a limited time starting August 18.

The collection, which is exclusive to U.S. and Canadian locations, will include six doughnuts total. Five are themed after specific Pokémon, including all three Gen 1 starters and two more Kanto region favorites. The sixth doughnut is an interpretation of the classic Poké Ball.

The doughnuts will be available for purchase individually or as a ‘Specialty Dozen Pack’ in select Krispy Kreme stores and through the Krispy Kreme app. A separate six-pack that skips out on Squirtle and Bulbasaur, replacing them with plain glazed doughnuts, will be available at other retailers like Walmart, Kroger, and Publix.

If you opt for the full Specialty Dozen, you’ll get a special, limited-edition Pokémon box. Krispy Kreme will also be offering five different Pokémon-themed cups for serving 'Original Glazed Gold Dots,' its version of doughnut holes.

That’s not all. Next Saturday, August 22, anyone who wears Pokémon merch to a participating Krispy Kreme location will get a free original glazed doughnut. It would have been nice if the freebie was Pokémon-themed, but a deal is a deal.

Preorders for the full 12-pack have already opened online , suggesting the doughnut company may have some concerns about potential stock. Yes, the Pokémon scalping problem now extends far beyond the trading card game. This may explain why a press release from Krispy Kreme only indicates that the Pokémon-themed collection will be available for a ‘limited time’ instead of having a clear end date.

If you'd like to plan your Pokémon journey sooner rather than later, you can check for participating locations on the Krispy Kreme website .

The Krispy Kreme collection is the latest addition to a long list of Pokémon’s 30th anniversary celebrations. Throughout 2026, we’ve seen merch collaborations with companies like Puma , some beautiful new guide books , and the release of a whopping 20 Pokemon-themed LEGO sets . The Pokémon trading card game will also be getting a special 30th anniversary product drop later this year.

While we won’t be getting a mainline Pokémon game, we did get our first look at Gen 10 , Winds and Waves, which is slated for 2027. We also got our hands on a new spin-off, Pokemon Pokopia, a Switch 2 exclusive we called an “enjoyable, personality-packed building simulator ” in our 9/10 review .

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: The Pokémon Center Just Dropped Its 2026 Halloween Collection
articles.summary: The Pokémon Center just dropped its Halloween Collection for 2026, with new apparel and decor featuring Gengar, Mimikyu, Umbreon, and... Golett?
articles.body:
The Pokémon Center just dropped its Halloween Collection for 2026. The new releases, which are already available to purchase online , include a mix of spooky-themed decorations, apparel, and kitchenware featuring fan-favorite Pokémon. The company is also seemingly getting ahead of the winter holiday season with new ornaments and snow globes.

Pok é mon Center Reveals 2026 Halloween Collection

The Pokémon Company has been celebrating the franchise’s 30th anniversary with a ridiculous amount of drops and announcements . This is one collection I always look forward to, however, because I’m a huge fan of the Ghost types that are typically featured.

It shouldn't come as any surprise that the Poké-star of this year’s drop is Gengar, who technically predates the Ghost type itself . That guy’s been getting a ridiculous amount of merch love recently. Other featured Pokémon include Mimikyu, Mewtwo, one of my all-time favorites, Misdreavus, and… Golett ? That one honestly caught me off guard.

On the decor side, I'm a big fan of the Umbreon and Espeon statues. I want the ethereal Eevee-lution duo guarding my house (apartment, but let me pretend) at all times. These are the same "made to look like stone" style as the previously released Cubone and Mimikyu statues that have been out of stock all year.

There’s a spread of more functional ‘pumpkin Pokémon’-themed items like tea-light holders and mugs, which I personally think are a bit jarring to look at. One thing that certainly isn't spooky is the Ditto candy holder. I, like presumably many people, recently rediscovered my adoration for Ditto through Pokémon Pokopia , and actually love how this thing is used to house tons of plushies in the promotional images .

The new apparel generally falls into the ‘cozy’ category, with a mix of sweaters, pajamas, and even bath robes almost entirely in adult sizes. The knit Gengar cardigan is a personal highlight, with a darker spiral pattern that's making me want to kick off my annual rewatch of The Nightmare Before Christmas.

Speaking of, the drop also includes a new batch of ornaments. I guess Halloween is close enough to the winter festivities.

The collection varies widely in terms of pricing, with the ornaments being the cheapest at $16.99, followed by Halloween-themed Pokémon window clings for $19.99. The most expensive new release is the luxurious Gengar bath robe, listed at $69.99.

You can see the full Halloween collection here , with all of the new additions already available to purchase.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: Pokémon x Crocs Collection Gets 3 More Clog Designs
articles.summary: After announcing the Poké Ball clog, Crocs has revealed three more upcoming designs featuring specific Pokémon.
articles.body:
After announcing the Poké Ball clog, Crocs has revealed three more upcoming designs featuring specific Pokémon.

Pikachu and Gengar will be getting standard clogs, listed at $79.99, while Jigglypuff is getting the platform clog treatment at $84.99. As of now, only the Pikachu style also has a kids size listing at the slightly cheaper price of $54.99. All of the new designs have an estimated release date of November 16.

Crocs Reveals 3 New Pokemon-Themed Clogs

The new Pokémon Crocs share relatively similar designs. The “face” of the Pokémon forms the front of the clog, with tailored patterns along the sides. Pikachu gets lightning bolts, Jigglypuff gets music notes, and Gengar gets, well, poisonous gas. Each also gets the Pokémon logo in a different metallic color on the ankle strap.

Jigglypuff Classic Platform Clog - Adult

Crocs had previously revealed the new collaboration with the Poké Ball-themed clog. That design will be available much sooner than the specific Pokemon clogs, with an estimated release date of August 28. Like Pikachu, the Poké Ball clog has listings in both adult and kid sizes, and will also be getting an additional toddler size .

At the time of writing, none of these upcoming releases are available for preorder. Instead, you can opt to give Crocs your email address or phone number for release updates. And whatever else they decide to send you.

If you happen to already be Croc-ed up, one thing that is already available for purchase is a collection of Pokémon-themed Jibbitz.

This drop is part of a continued collaboration between Crocs and Nintendo, and follows the release of both Animal Crossing clogs and a full Super Mario collection . It’s also one of many new releases that’s tied to Pokémon’s ongoing 30th anniversary. Even just in the world of shoes, Puma launched a collection earlier this year, and Adidas will be releasing a particularly wide spread of Pokémon-themed sneakers in September.

Outside of merch collaborations, the Pokémon trading card game is getting a whole set of 30th anniversary products . While the mainline games are skipping 2026, we did get our first trailer for Gen 10 , titled Winds and Waves, which will be released on the Switch 2 in 2027. We also got our hands on the cozy spin-off Pokémon Pokopia, which we think is pretty darn great .

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: 4 Penny Coffins Lets You Play 19th-Century Detective – Or a 10-Foot Demon Ripping Friends in Half
articles.summary: Other Ocean’s 4 Penny Coffins blends Among Us with Jack the Ripper in an 1888 Whitechapel social investigation game featuring 8-player and solo modes.
articles.body:
4 Penny Coffins is Jack the Ripper Meets Among Us, with a little bit of Psychonauts thrown in for fun. In the upcoming social investigation game, up to 8 players hunt a hidden murderer through lies, shifting alibis, and hard evidence . One of the players is the Ripper, a “gleeful demon concealed behind a facade of humanity,” stalking the winding alleys and rotting byways of 1888 London.

Ahead of IGN debuting 4 Penny Coffins’s gameplay teaser during gamescom 2026, which you can see in the player below, I spoke to Other Ocean Interactive Marketing Manager Jared Petty about the game’s mechanics, unique style (think stylized gore on top of monochromatic photographs), and Tim Schafer-inspired humor.

“It's a goddamn blast,” Petty says. “Four Penny Coffins; I've rarely had more fun playing a game with other people. A long time ago I was talking to Tim Schafer and I was asking him about humor in video games. Tim's opinion is that humor in video games is the easiest thing in the world because to paraphrase, ‘Our medium was built on a little yellow man that eats dots being chased by ghosts.’

“Humor and horror have always gone together so well. [Four Penny Coffins] having a multiplayer mode and being a very socially-oriented one creates all kinds of opportunities. Our philosophy was that the comical allows you to laugh so you don't scream.”

Petty says that the game’s humor translates directly into a multiplayer experience where you’re rewarded for trying to work together, but only if you want to.

“If you love trolling your friends, it's a beautiful game to play,” Petty says. “Our multiplayer ‘Ripper’ mode is class-based. All of you have different forensic abilities and are hunting the Ripper before they commit another murder. The fun part is one of you is the Ripper. So seven of you are using fingerprint and blood splatter analysis, photographing things, talking to witnesses, following photoprints, and doing all kinds of detective stuff, one of you screwing with that and occasionally turning into a giant 10-foot demon monster ripping people in half.”

Petty says that, while the “Ripper” mode allows you to work with your friends to figure out which one of you is 19th-century-inspired holy terror, the game’s solo “Magistrate” mode takes a different approach.

“It’s way more Sherlock Holmes-y,” Petty says. “Since you're there on your own, you've got a group of suspects locked up in a jail and you know one of them is the Ripper. You just don't know which one. So you're using tools from all the classes to go out and try to solve the mystery within a time limit. You make your choice and if you are wrong, you are penalized. You have three opportunities for your demerits. You take all your deductive reasoning and all your clues within that time limit, you bring it back, and you’ve got to hang somebody.”

Beyond the game mechanics, Petty says that the setting and style of 4 Penny Coffins is intended to help it stand out.

“I think you can see the influence in the graphic novel From Hell,” Petty says. “4 Penny Coffins is mostly a game that's in black and white until something [red and] violent happens. The game is built around an imaginative interpretation of a very dystopian time in 1888 Whitechapel London, which is where Jack the Ripper was. We wanted to create a sense of abstraction that was evocative of the age. We said, ‘What would an old woodcut newspaper brought to life look like? What would a moving grainy photo from the period look like?’ Our studio director, Chris Navarro, said ‘It's just gotta look cool.’”

When 4 Penny Coffins is released, Petty hopes players appreciate the care that went into crafting its story, mechanics, and style. But while the game promises tons of murder, violence, and mayhem, Petty says you don’t have to be a fan of the horror genre in order to enjoy it.

“It's just a great game for your friends and on your own. It's just really kind of a chill mental exercise, almost a puzzle. If you like puzzle games, you're going to love [it].”

For more from gamescom, be sure to check out everything that was revealed during Opening Night Live.

Michael Peyton is the Senior Editorial Director of Events & Entertainment at IGN, leading entertainment content and coverage of tentpole events including IGN Live, San Diego Comic Con, gamescom, and IGN Fan Fest. He's spent 20 years working in the games and entertainment industry, and his adventures have taken him everywhere from the Oscars to Japan to Buenos Aires, Argentina. Follow him on Bluesky @MichaelPeyton

articles.title: I Think I Love Silent Hill: Townfall, But I Also Saw So Much More! | gamescom 2026 - IGN
articles.summary: What's the best game at Gamescom 2026? There's some huge competition, including the return of The Witcher 3 (possibly the greatest game of all time), but for Jim's money? Silent Hill Townfall's take on a terrifying Scottish fishing village is the one to beat.Gamescom is the biggest gaming convention on Earth, in every sense. Physically, it's the size of a small town, with roughly the population of Swansea visiting every day from all over the globe. It's a dizzying celebration of gaming's past, present, and future. Join me on my first Gamescom with IGN for a window into what this behemoth is like to work in, and along the way we'll see some cool stuff, have a few laughs, and even preview some upcoming games: everything from Silent Hill Townfall to The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past!
articles.body:

articles.title: Grab Philips Shavers at a Steep Discount at Amazon Right Now
articles.summary: Save hundreds on Philips Shavers, including the Prestige Ultra model which is now better than half price.
articles.body:
If you’ve never used an electric shaver, you really are missing out. They’re smooth, they’re satisfying, and quite often they’ll net you a closer shave than a manual razor that gets duller in days.

Thankfully, Philips has an array of excellent options, and they’re seeing decent discounts right now at Amazon - including a whopping 51% off the i9000 Prestige Ultra, which sounds like it should be a car rather than something you use on your face.

We’ve already pointed out the OneBlade is seeing a great discount, but it’s not alone in that regard - and there’s something for just about any budget right now with these discounts at Amazon.

Take the Philips Electric Shaver Series 3000X , for example. It’s a sleek, comfortable device that would usually set you back £54.99, now just £44.99.

Not the biggest discount, admittedly, but for a first electric razor it’s really hard to go wrong. It offers a comfortable, clean shave that won’t leave marks despite using 27 self-sharpening blades, and is guaranteed for two years.

Those blades cup up to 55,000 times per minute to keep your shave steady and consistent, and the three heads can flex in four directions to match the contours of your face.

Next up is the Philips Electric Shaver Series 5000 , which, again, has 27 self-sharpening blades as well as a clip-on trimmer to maintain your ‘tache, trim your sideburns, or shape up your eyebrows (if you’re feeling brave).

Unlike the aforementioned model, its heads move 360 degrees to help with comfort while shaving, plus there’s a display that shows when it needs cleaning, charging, or the heads need replacing. It’s now £74.99, down 53% from its RRP of £159.99.

Looking for something even fancier for your face? The Philips Shaver i9000 Prestige Ultra (you know it’s good because ‘Prestige’ and ‘Ultra’ are in the name) usually sells for £649.99 - you could buy a whole new face for that.

Still, it’s an Amazon Exclusive, award-winning shaver that has a seven-year warranty and offers a 20% more precise shave than a manual razor. Its 360 rotating blades are ideal for cutting hair in all directions, and it includes SkinIQ Pro technology, which helps recommend changes in pressure and direction as you shave. It’s now down to £319.99, marking a 51% discount on that eye-watering RRP.

Whether it’s a big social occasion, a job interview, or just everyday maintenance, it’s clear there’s never been a better time to pick up a new shaver and revitalise your look.

Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's Added Verticality Adds EVEN MORE Things to Do | gamescom 2026 - IGN
articles.summary: The Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy is set to wrap up with 2027s Final Fantasy VII Revelation, and we are excited to finally battle the Weapons. We caught up with Naoki Hamaguchi, Game Director on FF7 Revelation, who gave us insights into how the Weapons are integrated into the story, Chadley's new role in the story, and what exactly he might be doing with all that combat training data...Final Fantasy VII Revelation is coming in early 2027 for PlayStation 5 (PS5), PC (Steam), and Xbox Series X|S.
articles.body:
The Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy is set to wrap up with 2027s Final Fantasy VII Revelation, and we are excited to finally battle the Weapons. We caught up with Naoki Hamaguchi, Game Director on FF7 Revelation, who gave us insights into how the Weapons are integrated into the story, Chadley's new role in the story, and what exactly he might be doing with all that combat training data...

Final Fantasy VII Revelation is coming in early 2027 for PlayStation 5 (PS5), PC (Steam), and Xbox Series X|S.

articles.title: Chess.com launched a poker site and is planning even more classic games
articles.summary: Chess.com’s new poker site, Gambit, is its first expansion, and now it’s working on launching sites for more games, like go, backgammon, and mahjong.
articles.body: Chess.com has done one thing, and one thing very well, for almost 20 years, but now it’s going beyond its domain name. The biggest name in online chess quietly launched its first companion site in beta back in May: Gambit, a free online poker website where players can learn the game without risking any real money. Now Gambit’s ready to really get the ball rolling with its first livestreamed event and collaborations with content creators, and Chess.com is planning to branch out into even more games from here. Chess.com’s chief growth officer, Albert Cheng, told The Verge the company chose poker for its first companion site because, like chess, it has learning and social elements on top of just playing the game. He also promised there will never be real-money gambling on Gambit, saying, “Real money is the problem we built Gambit to get away from, the whole industry makes money when beginners lose. We’d rather build a place where people can actually learn.” Gambit will look familiar to anyone who’s used Chess.com. It borrows the same design style and includes similar play modes, like bot matches, games with friends, tournaments, a review mode for studying your past games, and a learning mode. Gambit even includes Chess.com’s bot characters, with matching skill levels — I immediately recognized “Martin,” the lowest skill level bot from Chess.com, who is also the lowest skill level bot on Gambit. [Image: [Image: Chess.com also developed its own Elo-style rating system for Gambit. Cheng explained in an interview with The Verge that the rating system serves as the main motivator for players to improve: “You’re not gambling your own hard-earned money necessarily, so the stakes are lower from that standpoint, but you need something to counterbalance it that you care about, and that keeps the ecosystem in play, and keeps the poker that’s on Gambit reasonably high-quality.” The rating system is also the backbone of Gambit’s paid subscription for access to premium learning features, following the same model Chess.com uses. “Our primary business model of Chess.com is a subscription, but most people play Chess.com for free,” Cheng said. “They subscribe to get unlimited access to review their games and to get unlimited puzzles, lessons, et cetera.” A reliable rating system allows players to track their improvement, potentially motivating them to pay for those premium features. [Image: [Image: Rating systems are also at the heart of Chess’s next move. Chess.com is now looking to expand into even more classic games, including go, backgammon, and mahjong. Like Gambit, Chess.com is developing Elo-style rating systems for these games, as well. Cheng didn’t say when the new sites will launch but that “development is moving quite rapidly” on them, using the same playbook he used for Gambit. AI is a key reason Chess.com was finally able to expand into other games after nearly 20 years, according to Cheng. He and one other employee took Gambit from prototype to launch within a year, partly with help from AI, mainly for coding tasks. “I think the biggest advantage that it’s provided is essentially being able to read our existing codebase and our design system and apply consistent patterns to how we develop Chess.com over to a different platform and do so quickly,” Cheng said. He went on to add that there were also a lot of areas where AI struggles, such as brand and feature design. “I think that’s the best ultimate use of AI is that ultimately it’s going to be a blend, right?” Cheng said, adding, “Just because code is easier to write doesn’t mean that you just let it run on its own, but it certainly is a superpower in getting things off the ground.” Cheng also said the version of Gambit that’s live at the time of writing has “zero or close to zero” AI-created assets, which were used in early prototypes. According to Cheng, without help from AI, getting another site up and running would have required a bigger team or “would have been a lot more disruptive to the status quo of building and growing Chess.” Now that a “small, scrappy” team can get a new platform off the ground much faster, it’s opened the door for Chess.com to dip into more games, starting with poker. As Chess.com plans its next move, Cheng says they’re focusing on games with “both that classic durability plus the community around it,” like chess. Now that Gambit has launched, Cheng’s leaning into the community and social side of the platform more, following Chess.com’s lead, and getting content creators more involved. On August 31st at 12PM ET / 9AM PT, Gambit’s livestreaming its Gambit Cup for the first time on Twitch and YouTube with Chess.com co-founder Danny Rensch and chess content creator Alexandra Botez.

articles.title: PSA: Nintendo Switch 2 Gets a $50 Price Increase on Tuesday
articles.summary: Nintendo is raising the price of the Switch 2 to $500 on September 1, meaning this is your last chance to get one before the hike.
articles.body:
Compared to Sony and Microsoft , Nintendo has done an admirable job of keeping the price of the Switch 2 reasonably low amid rising component prices. But not even Mario is immune to market forces, and Nintendo is raising the Switch 2’s price by $50 on September 1. So, starting Tuesday, you’ll have to fork out $500 for a new hybrid console instead of the current MSRP of $450. In other words, if you’re thinking of picking up a Switch 2, this is your last chance to do so before the price hike.

When it comes to buying a Switch 2, you used to have more options than you do today. Previously, you could buy the console all by itself, or bundled with a game. There was even a bundle that let you choose among three first-party games. As we creep toward the price hike, however, all of the bundles have vanished from retailers. Your only reasonably priced option now is wither to buy a Switch 2 new or refurbished .

New Switch 2 consoles are available at all the usual retailers ( see at Amazon ). Refurbished Switch 2s are available at several retailers, but the best deal going right now is a “Grade A” refurbished unit at Woot for $399.99 . That’s $50 less than the current price of a new Switch 2, and it’s the best deal going if you don’t mind refurbished hardware.

Woot, by the way, is owned by Amazon, so you can rest assured it’s a legit retailer. I’ve bought many things from Woot and never had any problems.

Nintendo has announced it will introduce two new Switch 2 bundles after the price hike. One includes a copy of Mario Kart World . It will be available in “late September” and cost $549.99. The other includes Nintendo Switch Sports Resort . It will cost $529.99 and will be out October 22, the day that game comes out.

Both bundles will include three months of Nintendo Switch Online, and offer slight discounts versus buying the items individually. But neither bundle will save you more than $50, meaning your best bet is still to buy before the price goes up.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .
